title: Local derived completeness is unchanged by a unit times a positive power
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Let $a,b$ be global sections and suppose $a=u b^e$, where $u$ is an invertible global section and $e\geq1$. For $N\in D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], local derived $(a)$-completeness and local derived $(b)$-completeness are equivalent. Here local derived $(c)$-completeness means that, on each slice over $V$, $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_V}(\mathcal O_V[1/f],N|_V)=0$ for every $f\in(c)\mathcal O(V)$; localization is sheafified sectionwise and derived internal Hom is [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. More precisely, the reflection functors $R\mathcal Hom([\mathcal O\to\mathcal O[1/a]],-)$ and $R\mathcal Hom([\mathcal O\to\mathcal O[1/b]],-)$ are naturally isomorphic in a way carrying their actual augmentation-induced units to one another. The complexes are in degrees $0,1$ and augmented to $\mathcal O[0]$ by the degree-zero identity. No regularity or Noetherian hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 099B, lemma-derived-completion: augmented localization model for a principal ideal; comparison for a unit times a positive power is the explicit argument below.

proof.text: Objectwise, a = u b^e makes a invertible in O[1/b] and b invertible in O[1/a]. The localization universal property gives inverse coefficient-linear maps; uniqueness gives naturality under restriction. Sheafification carries these to an isomorphism commuting with the canonical maps from O.

proof.text: Use the identity in degree zero and the localization isomorphism in degree one to give an isomorphism between the actual two-term localization complexes, preserving their augmentations. Apply contravariant derived internal Hom to its inverse. This gives a natural isomorphism of the recorded completion functors; the augmentation equality implies equality of the actual completion units.

source.place: Tag 099B (lemma-derived-completion), and Tags 099E/099F (global extended Cech model and reflection).

proof.text: The image of multiplication by a section c is a finite-type ideal: the rank-one module has its singleton global generating section, and its epimorphism onto the image carries that generator to c on every slice. Take the existing global augmented extended Cech model for this ideal. Its local description compares each generating list with the singleton list (c). The singleton extended Cech complex is the actual two-term complex tensored with O[0]; the right unitor identifies it with the two-term complex and preserves augmentation. Restriction of the localization presheaf is the localization presheaf of the restricted section, and restriction commutes with sheafification. The resulting chain isomorphism has canonical identity comparison on the ring term. Passing to the derived category preserves its augmentation square by naturality of the derived-restriction comparison. Composing these comparisons yields a local extended Cech description for the actual two-term complex.

source.place: Tag 099B (lemma-derived-completion), and Tags 099E/099F (global extended Cech model and reflection).

proof.text: Apply the existing general extended Cech reflector properties to that local description. The output is locally derived complete, and precomposition with the specified augmentation-induced unit gives the required Hom bijection into each complete object.

source.place: Tag 099B (lemma-derived-completion), and Tags 099E/099F (global extended Cech model and reflection).

proof.text: For a reflection with complete outputs and the stated Hom bijection, an object is complete exactly when its unit is invertible. One direction transports completeness across the unit isomorphism. For the other, surjectivity supplies a retraction and injectivity at the complete reflected object proves the other inverse equation. Local derived completeness is invariant under isomorphism by functoriality of derived restriction and derived internal Hom. The unit-preserving natural comparison of step 2 therefore identifies completeness for a and b.
